definitions.explanation: Used to emphasize that something is genuine or to express sincere feelings.
Used to confirm or agree with something strongly.

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}にありがとう。
この{映画|えいが}は{本当|ほんとう}に{面白|おもしろ}かった。
{彼|かれ}は{本当|ほんとう}に{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}で、{初|はじ}めて{聞|き}いたときは{日本人|にほんじん}だと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: He is really good at Japanese — the first time I heard him speak, I thought he was Japanese.

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}にそう{思|おも}う。
「{今日|きょう}は{暑|あつ}いね。」「{本当|ほんとう}に。」
examples.english: "It's hot today, isn't it?" "It sure is."

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}に{大変|たいへん}でしたね。お{疲|つか}れさまでした。
examples.english: That was really tough, wasn't it. Good work.

notes:
{本当|ほんとう}に is the adverbial form of {本当|ほんとう} (truth/reality), used to emphasize sincerity or degree.

CASUAL FORMS:
- ほんとに: common casual contraction
- ほんと: very casual, often sentence-final
- マジで: slang equivalent (from {本気|まじ})

COMMON USES:
- {本当|ほんとう}にありがとう: thank you so much
- {本当|ほんとう}にすみません: I'm really sorry
- {本当|ほんとう}に{美味|おい}しい: really delicious

SIMILAR ADVERBS:
- {確|たし}かに: certainly, indeed (confirming facts)
- {実|じつ}に: truly, indeed (more formal/literary)
- とても: very (degree only, not sincerity)

NOTE:
{本当|ほんとう}に emphasizes both degree (really good) and genuineness (truly/sincerely), while とても only emphasizes degree.
